title: Genesys notification routing — admin portal

user.description: One person mapped to Genesys notification routing: the record the whole portal exists to keep correct. Identified to the operator by name and email; tied to Genesys by the Dynamic Group ID.

relations.why: every read and write of a user is scoped through the signed-in identity's role and area — row-level access is the product's second requirement

actions.constraint: an Area Admin only ever sees their own area's users — not even the other areas' names or counts
an Area Admin's Area field is pre-filled and disabled; the Superuser chooses among all five
same area scoping as add; the store refuses what the UI never offers
confirmation first, destructive confirm colour — it may never look like a save

identity.description: Who is operating the portal: the Superuser, or one Area Admin per area. Not a record to manage but the lens every other record is read through — which is why it is an object and not a session detail.

actions.constraint: landing goes straight to the user list — no dashboard between (requirement 4.1)
lives in the UserMenu at the header's far end, where every app here puts it

vocabularies.area: five fixed values. Fails the litmus test: no screen shows an area as an instance with a life of its own — it is the scope on a user and on an identity.
vocabularies.organization: eight fixed values plus a user-defined number; a field on the user, nothing more.
vocabularies.recipientRole: 21 fixed values — long enough for a Combobox, still a vocabulary: nobody views or edits a recipient role itself.

openQuestions: The real deployment authenticates against the corporate identity provider; whether area arrives as a claim or from the portal's records is a backend decision this model inherits from the login spec.

If a deployment ever manages areas themselves (rename, add a sixth), area stops being a vocabulary and becomes an object with its own collection screen — that is the condition that reopens this split.
